problem:
Which of the following functions are piecewise continuous on $x\in [-5,\infty ).$

$$
f(x)=⌈x⌉,\,g(x)=u(x+1)+u(x+4),\,h(x)=\operatorname{tan}⁡x
$$

Note that $u(x)$ is the unit step function, and $⌈x⌉$ is the ceiling function.

examples.knowledge_point: Identifying Piecewise-Continuous Functions Over Infinite Intervals
examples.problem:
Which of the following functions are piecewise continuous on $x\in [0,\infty).$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={\begin{aligned}1,\, & ⌈x⌉\text{ is even} \\ -1,\, & ⌈x⌉\text{ is odd}\end{aligned} \\ g(x) & =u(x-1)+u\,(x-\frac{1}{2})+u\,(x-\frac{1}{3})+⋯ \\ h(x) & =⌈\frac{x}{2}⌉\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $u(x)$ is the unit step function, and $\lceil x \rceil$ is the ceiling function.
examples.worked_solution:
Suppose $I\subseteq \mathbb R.$ A function $f: I \to \mathbb R$ is piecewise continuous on $I$ if it is piecewise continuous on every closed and bounded subinterval $[a,b]\subset I.$

With that in mind, let's examine each function.

- The function $f(x)$ is piecewise continuous over $x\in [0,\infty).$ The function has jump discontinuities at $x=1,2,3,\ldots,$ and any closed interval $[a,b]\subset [0,\infty)$ will contain finitely many discontinuities.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14042449/assets/3ce7aa18de332c3eb1bc57b6bf7c50acf1573717d642c731a18a85f4f9fb813a.png)

- The function $g(x)$ is not piecewise continuous over $x\in [0,\infty).$ Consider the closed subinterval $x\in [0,1].$ Notice that the function has jump discontinuities at $x=1,\dfrac12,\dfrac13,\dfrac14,\ldots,$ so it has infinitely many discontinuities on this closed interval.

- The function $h(x)$ is piecewise continuous over $x\in [0,\infty).$ The function has jump discontinuities at $x=0,2,4,\ldots,$ and any closed interval $[a,b]\subset [0,\infty)$ will contain finitely many discontinuities.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14042449/assets/9a5cc55dc36927437d16d09b4e491305efebac9d9a8995a741d62b6395a101bd.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "$f$ and $h$ only."

feedback.problem:
Which of the following functions are piecewise continuous on $x\in [0,2].$

$$
f(x)=\frac{1}{x-1},\,g(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x,\,h(x)={\begin{aligned}2x+1,\, & x<1 \\ {x}^{2}+1,\, & x\ge 1.\end{aligned}
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
A function $f(x)$ is piecewise continuous on $x\in [a,b]$ if

- it is continuous on $[a,b]$ except at finitely many points, and

- at each point of discontinuity, the one-sided limits exist and are finite.

In other words, there can only be finitely many discontinuities, and each of them must be either a point or a jump discontinuity.

With that in mind, let's examine each function.

- The function $f(x)$ is not piecewise continuous over $x\in [0,2]$ since the one-sided limits at $x=1$ are infinite:

$$
{lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}f(x)=-\infty ,\,{lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}f(x)=+\infty 
$$

- The function $g(x)$ is piecewise continuous over $x\in [0,2]$ since it is continuous over $x\in [0,2].$

- The function $h(x)$ is piecewise continuous over $x\in [0,2]$ since it is continuous over $x\in [0,2]$ except at the point $x=1,$ where the one-sided limits exist and are finite:

$$
{lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}h(x)=3,\,{lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}h(x)=2
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$g$ and $h$ only."
